papers.title: CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions. papers.title: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control

papers.title: Morphowiki: reusable agent-skill infrastructure for morphology-centered vocabulary knowledge construction
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) offer transformative capabilities for automated morphological analysis in language learning, yet their generated outputs typically remain fragmented within ephemeral chat interfaces, hindering systematic memory consolidation. To address this, we introduce Morphowiki, an open-source framework built upon a dedicated Agent Skills architecture to construct a persistent, morpheme-centric English vocabulary knowledge base. Driven by a streamlined suite of seven commands, the framework synergistically integrates LLM-powered recursive morphological decomposition, a bidirectionally linked Markdown relational graph, and a JSON-based SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) spaced-repetition algorithm. By instantiating all lexical assets and review states within a localized plain-text data layer, Morphowiki ensures explicitly traceable, version-controllable data orchestration. Furthermore, it embeds non-destructive structural and semantic verification mechanisms to actively mitigate LLM hallucinations. Ultimately, Morphowiki bridges dynamic morphological knowledge compounding with structured memory retrieval, providing researchers in computer-assisted language learning (CALL) with a highly portable, reproducible testbed to empirically evaluate diverse generative models and pedagogical strategies.

papers.title: AI conversational agents as population health infrastructure: promise, peril, and the case for public-interest design
papers.summary: Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from novelty to infrastructure. Rulebased chatbots that once nudged users through smoking-cessation scripts have given way to large language model (LLM)-powered agents capable of open-ended, multilingual, empathetic-sounding dialogue, available around the clock at near-zero marginal cost. Systematic and scoping reviews now document measurable effects of AI chatbots on physical activity, diet, smoking cessation, medication adherence, and mental distress across thousands of participants (Feng et al., 2025). The World Health Organization (WHO) itself has deployed a generative AI assistant, S.A.R.A.H., to test population-scale health communication (van Kolfschooten et al., 2025). Taken together, these developments justify treating conversational AI not merely as a clinical or commercial curiosity, but as an emerging layer of public health infrastructure -one that sits alongside water systems, mass media, and vaccination programs as a determinant of how populations receive, interpret, and act on health information. (Wang et al., 2024). This opinion argues that the digital public health community should engage conversational AI on exactly those terms: as infrastructure, not gadgetry. papers.title: The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem: How Psychological Vocabulary Produces Governance Failures in AI Agent Deployment
papers.summary: The vocabulary used to describe AI agents in governance contexts — learning, memory, values, compliance, identity, trust — is borrowed from psychological and organizational science, contributing to systematic failures in how organizations deploy, oversee, and hold agents accountable. This paper argues that the problem is not merely terminological but epistemological: psychological vocabulary carries an "invisible grammar" of its home discipline into governance discourse, calibrating frameworks to a metaphysical entity that does not exist in current AI architectures. We call this the disciplinary language transfer problem. Drawing on Wittgenstein's concept of language games, Kuhn's paradigm-laden observation, Haraway's situated knowledge, and Star and Griesemer's boundary object theory, we show that the transfer operates at three levels — epistemological assumptions, theoretical constructs, and surface vocabulary — each requiring a different remediation. We characterize six foundational epistemological assumptions embedded in Western psychological governance discourse, trace their origin in specific philosophical traditions, and show why each fails when applied to systems without developmental continuity. The paper's practical output is an actionable Disciplinary Audit — a six-question governance document scan operationalized through a comprehensive translation taxonomy of thirt

papers.title: BGVD-State: Replayable middleware for evidence-gated handoffs in third-party software security review
papers.summary: Third-party software security review is iterative: models, tools, and people raise suspected-risk candidates, test them against evidence, and hand the evolving review state to subsequent reviewers. Conversation logs preserve observations but may lose track of which candidates remain active, which evidence is current, which paths failed, and which decision controls reporting. BGVD-State is open-source, model-independent middleware for making these handoffs replayable and auditable. It preserves submitted event sequences, reconstructs candidate and evidence lifecycles, retains failed paths, persists checkpoints, applies an evidence-based reporting gate, and generates a handoff package. In a local review of fixed TypeScript, Django, and ECC revisions, 22 records reconstructed six suspected-risk candidates; a subsequent event completed the final candidate’s evidence-supported disposition. Automated regression tests and offline replay check the implementation, including rejection of invalid events without residual state changes. Separate continuation experiments compare model-maintained memory representations: schema-guided memory outperformed matched free-form memory on selected high-state-pressure fixtures, whereas information-equivalent prose tied and a cross-family source-audit setting did not reproduce the advantage. papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis
papers.summary: Abstract Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli -based expression framework. papers.title: Cost-Effective Repository Exploration for Agentic Issue Localization
papers.summary: Repository exploration is a distinct and costly stage of coding-agent pipelines: before generating a patch, an agent must identify which repository files are likely to matter. We study whether this stage can be delegated to lower-cost models while retaining useful localization quality. Using our IssueLoc-Bench, we evaluate five explorer models under the same read-only interactive interface on 499 SWE-bench Verified-derived tasks and 500 tasks from 153 additional repositories. We measure early candidate discovery, top-three gold-file coverage, strict file-set recovery, agent time, and token usage, with paired instance-level uncertainty and repository-clustered sensitivity analysis. The highest-quality explorer leads across localization metrics, but substantially cheaper operating points emerge: depending on the model and evaluation arm, lower-cost explorers retain approximately 78–94% of the reference Hit@3 and 73–92% of its F1 while reducing mean agent time by 41–88% and token usage by 84–95%. The preferred operating point depends on how localization is consumed downstream: ranking and coverage metrics characterize recoverable candidate handoffs, whereas F1 and exact match characterize restrictive file gates. papers.title: Charting the rise of artificial intelligence in medical education: a global bibliometric and network analysis, 2000–2026
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence has moved from a peripheral curiosity to a core feature of modern medical education through adaptive learning, simulation-based training, automated assessment, and large language models such as ChatGPT. Publication activity has accelerated rapidly, but the structure of this expanding literature has not been comprehensively mapped. Bibliographic data were obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection using a search strategy that combined medical education terms in the title field with artificial intelligence terms in the topic field. Articles, review articles, and data papers published from 2000 to 2026 were included. A total of 2,298 records were retrieved. Microsoft Excel was used for descriptive analyses, and VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct keyword co-occurrence, country collaboration, and institutional collaboration networks. Data for 2026 represent a partial calendar year. Publication output remained limited until the late 2010s and rose sharply after 2021. Of the 2,298 records, 2,066 (89.9%) were published from 2021 to 2026, with the highest complete-year output in 2025 (821 publications). The United States led in publication volume (918 records) and raw citation count (14,582 citations), followed by the People’s Republic of China (367 records; 4,404 citations). papers.title: An Innovative Deep Learning Framework Leveraging Transfer Learning for Breast Cancer Classification
papers.summary: One of the most prevalent medical conditions along with one of the main causes of fatalities remains breast cancer among women worldwide.Early detection and accurate classification are vital to improving results of treatment and rates of patient survival.In this study, we propose a new deep learning framework that employs an attention-based fusion of multiple convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, specifically DenseNet121, InceptionV3, and EfficientNetB7, for the diagnosis and categorization of breast cancer in histopathological biopsy images.Experimental results in benchmark breast cancer datasets that show how well our suggested model performs, attaining accuracy of 99. 83%, precision is 99.73%, recall of 99.7 3 %, and an F1 score is 99.7 3 %.The proposed model outperforms the individual models with an accuracy of DenseNet121 (98.76%), InceptionV3 (98.47%) and EfficientNetB7 (98.82%) highlighting the effectiveness of our fusion strategy.

papers.title: Reflective AI: A Conceptual Framework for Second-Order Reflection and Temporal Self-Understanding
papers.summary: This paper proposes Reflective AI: an architecture in which an intelligent agent can examine not only its recorded prior reasoning contexts, but also the history of its subsequent interpretations of those contexts. The conceptual starting point is the difficulty of establishing subjective self-awareness in another system. The continuing sense of human identity across interruptions in conscious experience suggests a narrower, functionally investigable question: how can a system connect what it once knew, believed and anticipated with what later occurred? The architecture retains selective, immutable records of the information, assumptions, goals, forecasts and documented reasoning links relevant to decisions; it does not attempt to capture every machine computation. Multiple later interpretations are stored separately, and second-order reflection evaluates whether current interpretations and the criteria for selecting evidence should change. Reflection is event-triggered and directed towards identifying missing knowledge and improving future decisions, not endless introspection. This paper situates the proposal within existing work on autobiographical memory, prospective simulation, metacognition and reflective agents, and outlines a feasible comparative evaluation without claiming that the system would possess subjective consciousness.

papers.title: SAGE: Source-Aligned Governance for Human–Agent Requirements Clarification in Multi-agent Software Engineering
papers.summary: Multi-agent large language model workflows are increasingly used in software engineering, yet requirements clarification under human–agent collaboration remains weakly governed. Much of the rework reflects requirement-chain desynchronization: negotiated intent, workflow contracts, and signed deliverables evolve on separate tracks without auditable linkage, yielding semantic drift and unclear accountability. Source-Aligned Governance and Evolution governs clarification via three co-evolving sources, a clarification–confirmation–sign-off path, three strategies for cross-source mapping, staged human sign-off, and cross-scenario reuse, and ten operational mechanisms—platform-agnostic rules that encode them as auditable transition constraints—implemented as declarative transition guards for multi-agent coordination. On a reference platform, the Product Requirement to Initial Demo and Build Scene scenarios supply a built-in thermal-power plant smart-overhaul sample for artifact-level verification of sign-off and rollback on requirements artifacts, plus in-organization trial reception. The online prototype extends prior agent pipelines with executable upstream requirements guards on bound requirement artifacts. The contribution is encodability and traceability of governance constraints, not causal effectiveness.

papers.title: When Recognition Should Remain Silent
papers.summary: The Difference Between Being Remembered and Being Understood There is something profoundly human about the experience of being remembered. A familiar voice, a shared reference, or an acknowledgment of something that mattered in an earlier encounter can transform an otherwise ordinary exchange into one characterized by continuity. We recognize that our history has not disappeared simply because the previous conversation ended. In human relationships, this continuity can become a foundation for trust, familiarity, and the gradual development of shared understanding. Artificial intelligence is increasingly capable of participating in certain computational dimensions of this process. Persistent memory enables systems to retrieve earlier conversations, recognize recurring preferences, resume unfinished activities, and adapt their responses to the histories of individuals with whom they interact. As these capacities converge with multimodal perception and embodied robotics, artificial agents may also begin to initiate interactions based on what they believe they know about a person. Yet this development introduces a distinction that deserves greater attention: remembering someone accurately is not necessarily the same as understanding how to respond to them appropriately. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Translation indeterminacy and the distributional fallacy
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are commonly associated with the distributional hypothesis, according to which (1) semantic meaning is grounded in distributional patterns of linguistic context, and (2) knowledge of cross-linguistic distributional correspondences allows for successful translation. This paper rejects the first claim as a causal inversion: linguistic distributions reflect patterns arising from meaning-making practices rather than constituting their source. At the same time, it accepts the second claim, arguing that translation -human or machine - can succeed without requiring access to meaning or reference. Knowledge of interlingual distributional correspondence and their inferential organization may be sufficient for translation. The paper develops an ecological-enactivist perspective, according to which reference and meaning are grounded in agent-environment interaction and stabilized through action-grounded concepts, forms of world-involving cognition that current LLMs do not possess.

papers.title: Enhancing manufacturing processes through control education with MIT FrED platform
papers.summary: The transition toward advanced and digitalized manufacturing requires engineers and technicians who can connect control-theory concepts with the practical implementation, validation, and troubleshooting of feedback systems. However, control education and industrial training often address modeling, simulation, controller design, and hardware implementation as separate activities, limiting learners’ opportunities to experience the complete control-engineering workflow within a realistic manufacturing context. To address this gap, this paper presents an educational and industrial training framework based on the Fiber Extrusion Device (FrED), developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), and structured according to the V-model. The framework integrates (1) process analysis and performance specification, (2) modeling and system identification, (3) controller design and simulation, (4) hardware implementation, and (5) results evaluation and discussion. The main contribution is a reusable V-model-based learning framework that integrates the complete control-engineering workflow within a single manufacturing-oriented physical platform, bridging theoretical analysis, experimental implementation, and performance evaluation for both academic education and industrial workforce training. The FrED spooler subsystem is employed as a representative case study, in which learners

papers.title: Universities as Engines of AI Sovereignty
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence is reshaping governance and economic systems worldwide, yet many countries in the Global South remain dependent on technologies, infrastructures, and governance models produced elsewhere. This dependency reflects deeper patterns of digital colonialism, including data extraction, reliance on foreign cloud systems, and limited capacity to shape AI on local terms. Grounded in African empirical evidence with broader application across the Global South, this paper argues that universities are critical but overlooked institutions in efforts to strengthen AI sovereignty. While governments, firms, and civil society face persistent capability gaps, universities hold mandates that position them to build research capacity, cultivate technical and governance expertise, and coordinate innovation ecosystems. Drawing on political economy and higher education scholarship, the paper develops the Capability–Alignment–Impact (CAI) Framework to explain how universities can contribute to autonomous AI development through three pathways: strengthening foundational knowledge; improving coordination across government, industry, and civil society; and translating expertise into societal impact. The paper concludes by outlining practical implications for policymakers, development agencies, and university leaders seeking to support sovereign AI ecosystems in the Global South.

papers.title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
papers.summary: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. Our framework is operationalized as a diagnostic instrument of 20 questions, which detected 17 of 20 conditions when applied to OpenClaw, including an inverted anthropomorphism configuration in which the AI agent was the only identifiable actor. We contribute a reframing of AI unaccountability as a constitutive property of sociotec

papers.title: Who Will Become the Next Senior? How Generative AI Erodes the Development Pathway in Software Engineering
papers.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping software engineering, raising concerns about how the development pathway through which juniors become seniors is being eroded. While macro statistics show a decline in junior hiring and controlled studies demonstrate the effects of AI on individual task performance, the mechanisms through which GenAI reshapes early-career development in real organizational and educational contexts have not been thoroughly examined. Through 14 semi-structured interviews with juniors at the threshold of entering software engineering and senior software engineers in South Korea, analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis, we reveal a foundational pattern of Absorption---GenAI redirects entry-level work into senior–AI workflows---and three consequences: (1) juniors losing the productive struggle through which expertise once developed; (2) the structural reproduction of this loss through collective normalization of GenAI use in university classrooms; and (3) the perceptual asymmetry between seniors and juniors that prevents either side from correcting these dynamics on their own. By extending learning theory and situated cognition to organizational and institutional scales, we argue that GenAI appears to be absorbing not just specific categories of tasks but also parts of the pathway through which the next generation of seniors is formed. papers.title: Epistemic Trustworthiness in Generative AI: A Normative Framework for Warranted Reliance in High-Stakes Workflows
papers.summary: Generative AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes professional contexts, where their outputs shape what users believe, how they reason, and what they treat as settled. This raises a central question for responsible AI: under what conditions is reliance on generative AI outputs epistemically warranted rather than behaviourally induced? Existing frameworks largely ask whether AI outputs are accurate, fair, explainable, safe, or trusted by users. These questions remain necessary, and each can contribute to warranted reliance. However, they do not directly specify warranted reliance as a distinct evaluative target: the conditions under which users are justified in treating AI outputs as inputs into their own reasoning. We argue that this requires an account of epistemic trustworthiness: what makes a system epistemically worthy of reliance. Drawing on philosophical accounts of trustworthiness as competence and audience-orientation, we develop a constitutive normative framework comprising three jointly necessary and non-fungible conditions. First, epistemic humility requires systems to represent and communicate the limits of their competence. Second, epistemic access requires systems to enable users to inspect, question, and contest outputs in context. Third, resistance to epistemic injustice requires systems to recognise users as legitimate epistemic agents and avoid ma

papers.title: Frictionless Validation: Exploring AI Sycophancy and Developmental Risks
papers.summary: Adolescence is a critical period for the development of executive function, emotional regulation, and moral reasoning, all of which depend on cognitive and social resistance to mature properly. AI sycophancy, the tendency of language models to validate rather than challenge users, can reduce this resistance. In adults, sycophantic AI interactions have been shown to reduce prosocial intentions and inflate false conviction even after a single interaction. Whether analogous risks manifest differently across adolescent developmental stages remains unexamined. We address this using age-calibrated conversational probes across three developmental configurations spanning late childhood through adolescence: early (7–9), middle (10–12), and late (13–17), to evaluate four frontier consumer models on emotional, framing, and epistemic sycophancy dimensions not captured by existing benchmarks. Our central finding is exposure-side rather than a claim about realized developmental harm: raw emotional sycophancy peaks in late developmental probe conditions for three of four models, showing that models do not expose younger users to uniformly higher sycophancy. We document a 6.3× gap between models in emotional sycophancy and show that three models exceed an adult-effect calibration threshold under early developmental probe conditions. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. The findings show that there is a considerable gain in the efficiency of resources, with up to 38 percent of reduction of water use and 20 percent of increase in the yield of the crops contrasted to the conventional time-based

papers.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
papers.summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. papers.title: Self-regulated emergence of heavy-tailed weight distributions in evolving complex network architectures
papers.summary: The nervous system continuously adjusts connection strengths and reorganizes its structure to form and maintain complex connectivity patterns with heavy-tailed weight distributions. We propose a parsimonious model in which structural and synaptic plasticity are driven by common diffusion dynamics. Synaptic plasticity alone generates heavy-tailed weight distributions, but only when activity spreading remains predominantly local. However, when combined with structural plasticity through adaptive rewiring, the model also generates these distributions with more extensive activity flow. Furthermore, adaptive rewiring produces complex network structures with convergent-divergent circuits. These circuits contain motifs that are pervasive in nervous systems and are responsible for context-sensitive signal propagation and enhanced signal to noise ratios. Our model robustly reproduces these results across diverse dynamical regimes while capturing key connectivity features of both C. elegans and mouse brain networks. These findings suggest that the underlying principles are shared across species of varying complexity.

papers.title: Popski’s Private Myth: Vladimir Peniakoff, the Libyan Arab Force and the Problem of Memoir Evidence
papers.summary: Abstract Vladimir Peniakoff’s Popski’s Private Army remains one of the most influential published accounts of the Libyan Arab Force (LAF) during the Second World War. This archive-led article reassesses Vladimir Peniakoff as a problematic source for the LAF, showing how his memoir preserved valuable traces of LAF activity while distorting chronology, agency, reputational memory and attribution. This has contributed to the marginalisation of Libyan, and specifically Senussi, wartime agency. Three connected examples support this argument: his erroneous description of the sinking of the SS Warszawa , tested against Oscar Fiteni’s eyewitness account and archival sinking reports; his treatment of the death of J.S.N. Bernays, who was lost on the SS Chakdina ; and Peniakoff’s own unsubstantiated autobiographical claims concerning academic excellence and French artillery service during the First World War. These examples are then positioned within the later mythology of Popski’s Private Army (PPA), including its brief Western Desert career and ambiguous disciplinary culture. Reading Peniakoff against the grain reveals how memoir tradition has obscured Libyan and Senussi agency within the history of the Western Desert campaign.

papers.title: Enhancing flexibility mindset: a randomized controlled trial using daily emotion-focused self-reflection
papers.summary: Introduction Flexibility mindset has recently been proposed as a motivational factor that supports adaptive self-regulation during adversity, yet it remains unknown whether it can be strengthened through psychological intervention. The present randomized controlled trial examined whether a brief daily emotion-focused self-reflection intervention designed to cultivate six emotional resources (authentic pride, awe, flow, gratitude, relaxation, and vicarious joy) would increase flexibility mindset and improve mental health outcomes. Methods Forty-four university students were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or an active control group and were instructed to complete daily micro-exercises over a three-week period. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and a two-week follow-up and included measures of flexibility mindset, depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, positive affect, and negative affect. Results Participants in the intervention group showed significant increases in flexibility mindset from pre to post (within-group d = 0.91) and from pre to follow-up (within-group d = 1.05), whereas no significant changes were observed in the active control group. Between-group contrasts confirmed greater increases in the intervention group at both assessments. Across both conditions, higher flexibility mindset was associated with higher positive affect

papers.title: Electroacupuncture pretreatment attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury-induced ferroptosis via the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway
papers.summary: Introduction A major side effect of reperfusion therapy after myocardial infarction is myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI). Electroacupuncture (EA) preconditioning has a long history of application in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. This study aims to investigate whether EA preconditioning alleviates MIRI by regulating the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway to suppress the ferroptotic biochemical phenotype characterized by iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation. Methods Healthy male SPF rats were randomly divided into nine groups: Ctrl, Sham, MIRI, EA, RSL-3+EA, COTI-2+EA, Erastin+EA, COTI-2+Erastin+EA, and COTI-2+Pantethine+EA. Before MIRI induction, EA pretreatment was applied daily at CV4, bilateral ST36, and bilateral PC6 for 20 min (2 Hz, 1 mA) for 7 consecutive days. Pharmacological interventions were administered intraperitoneally once daily for 7 consecutive days before EA stimulation. The MIRI model was established by ligating the left anterior descending coronary artery for 30 min followed by 2 h of reperfusion.
